subject: Estimating detection probability with predict-function in pcountOpen

messages.author: badfb066fb6a2eba
messages.subject: Estimating detection probability with predict-function in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi everybody,

when I try to estimate abundance using function

abundance_2013 <- predict(fm1_2013_p_Elev_LocTyp_Logg13_Pred13_psi_Elev_LocTyp_Logg13_Pred13_zip,
                                       type = "state")

I get exactly 60 estimated values for all of my 60 locations.


But when I try to use almost the same function for estimating detection probability like

detection_probability_2013 <- predict(fm1_2013_p_Elev_LocTyp_Logg13_Pred13_psi_Elev_LocTyp_Logg13_Pred13_zip,
                                                       type = "det")

I get 1736 estimates and I don't have an idea why this happens.


What do I have to do to get exactly 60 estimates for detection propability?


Cheers,
Monika

messages.author: 58a62321f08f30f8
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Estimating detection probability with predict-function in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi Monika,

 

When you predict from the detection model, you will get a prediction for each visit to each site, and therefore more that the number of sites. If you have no time varying (occasion-specific) covariates, then you should see some repeats in the predictions and all sites will have the same value – easy to pick site specific values in that case. If, on the other hand, you have covariates on detectability, you would need to decide what values of those covariates you want to make predictions for. You would do this by providing a new data frame for prediction.

 

Chris
